claim: Mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) are multipotent cells that demonstrate therapeutic potential for the treatment of acute and chronic inflammatory-mediated conditions.
source: Mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) are multipotent cells that demonstrate therapeutic potential for the treatment of acute and chronic inflammatory-mediated conditions.
evidence: This is a general statement about MSC therapeutic potential, supported by established scientific knowledge in the field.

claim: Some studies suggest that MSCs may lose their functionality with cryopreservation which could render them non-efficacious.
source: Although controversial, some studies suggest that MSCs may lose their functionality with cryopreservation which could render them non-efficacious.
evidence: This claim references existing studies in the literature, indicated by the phrase 'some studies suggest'.

claim: A total of 257 in vivo pre-clinical efficacy experiments represented 101 distinct outcome measures.
source: A total of 257 in vivo pre-clinical efficacy experiments represented 101 distinct outcome measures.
evidence: This is a direct report of data collected and analyzed in the systematic review.

claim: Of the 257 in vivo pre-clinical efficacy outcomes, 2.3% (6/257) were significantly different at the 0.05 level or less.
source: Of these outcomes, 2.3% (6/257) were significantly different at the 0.05 level or less; 2 favoured freshly cultured and 4 favoured cryopreserved MSCs.
evidence: This is a statistical finding from the systematic review data analysis.

claim: Of the 6 significantly different in vivo outcomes, 2 favoured freshly cultured and 4 favoured cryopreserved MSCs.
source: Of these outcomes, 2.3% (6/257) were significantly different at the 0.05 level or less; 2 favoured freshly cultured and 4 favoured cryopreserved MSCs.
evidence: This is a direct report of the direction of effects from the data analysis.

claim: A total of 68 in vitro experiments represented 32 different potency measures.
source: A total of 68 in vitro experiments represented 32 different potency measures; 13% (9/68) of the experiments were significantly different at the 0.05 level or less, with seven experiments favouring freshly cultured MSC and two favouring cryopreserved MSCs.
evidence: This is a direct report of data collected in the systematic review.

claim: 13% (9/68) of the in vitro experiments were significantly different at the 0.05 level or less.
source: A total of 68 in vitro experiments represented 32 different potency measures; 13% (9/68) of the experiments were significantly different at the 0.05 level or less, with seven experiments favouring freshly cultured MSC and two favouring cryopreserved MSCs.
evidence: This is a statistical finding from the systematic review data analysis.

claim: Of the 9 significantly different in vitro experiments, seven favoured freshly cultured MSC and two favoured cryopreserved MSCs.
source: A total of 68 in vitro experiments represented 32 different potency measures; 13% (9/68) of the experiments were significantly different at the 0.05 level or less, with seven experiments favouring freshly cultured MSC and two favouring cryopreserved MSCs.
evidence: This is a direct report of the direction of effects from the data analysis.

claim: The majority of preclinical primary in vivo efficacy and secondary in vitro potency outcomes were not significantly different (p<0.05) between freshly cultured and cryopreserved MSCs.
source: The majority of preclinical primary in vivo efficacy and secondary in vitro potency outcomes were not significantly different (p<0.05) between freshly cultured and cryopreserved MSCs.
evidence: This is the main conclusion drawn from the systematic review data analysis.

claim: MSCs are multipotent stem cells that can be isolated from many adult tissues (e.g. bone marrow, adipose tissue).
source: Mesenchymal stromal cells (mesenchymal stem cells; MSCs) are multipotent stem cells that can be isolated from many adult tissues (e.g. bone marrow, adipose tissue) (Pittenger et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Pittenger et al., 2019.

claim: MSCs have been studied in clinical trials for almost two decades.
source: MSCs have been studied in clinical trials for almost two decades (Koç et al., 2000), and have since been implicated in use for diverse conditions (Gomez-Salazar et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Koç et al., 2000 and Gomez-Salazar et al., 2020.

claim: MSCs release growth factors and cytokines along with extracellular vesicles to activate cell proliferation, prevent apoptosis, and ultimately improve regenerative response.
source: MSCs release growth factors and cytokines along with extracellular vesicles to activate cell proliferation, prevent apoptosis, and ultimately improve regenerative response (Pittenger et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Pittenger et al., 2019.

claim: MSCs may modulate the immune response by decreasing inflammation, reducing scar formation, increasing pathogen clearance, altering endothelial permeability, and improving mitochondrial dysfunction as demonstrated in different pre-clinical models of inflammation.
source: MSCs may also modulate the immune response by decreasing inflammation, reducing scar formation, increasing pathogen clearance, altering endothelial permeability, and improving mitochondrial dysfunction as demonstrated in different pre-clinical models of inflammation (Fish and Hajjar, 2015; Hoogduijn et al., 2010; Gupta et al., 2012; Islam et al., 2012; Li et al., 2018; Tsubokawa et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to pre-clinical studies.

claim: The mechanism for how MSCs modulate inflammation and promote healing is not yet completely understood.
source: The mechanism for how MSCs modulate inflammation and promote healing is not yet completely understood; however, the observed effect may be mediated by both the direct contact with immune cells and release of soluble factors (Caplan, 2009; Shi et al., 2012; Souza-Moreira et al., 2022).
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of scientific knowledge, supported by citations.

claim: The observed effect of MSCs may be mediated by both the direct contact with immune cells and release of soluble factors.
source: The mechanism for how MSCs modulate inflammation and promote healing is not yet completely understood; however, the observed effect may be mediated by both the direct contact with immune cells and release of soluble factors (Caplan, 2009; Shi et al., 2012; Souza-Moreira et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to relevant studies.

claim: As of March 10, 2022, 1,097 active trials involving MSCs were registered on clinicaltrials.gov.
source: Moreover, as of March 10, 2022, 1,097 active trials involving MSCs were registered (https://www.clinicaltrials.gov).
evidence: This is a factual statement based on data from a clinical trials registry.

claim: In a recent systematic review of the safety of MSCs in 55 randomized clinical trials, only 15 (27%) used cryopreserved cells.
source: In a recent systematic review of the safety of MSCs in 55 randomized clinical trials, only 15 (27%) used cryopreserved cells (Thompson et al., 2020), potentially due to the concern that cryopreserved MSCs may lose some of their functionality (Galipeau et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Thompson et al., 2020.

claim: Some in vitro studies demonstrate a negative impact of cryopreservation on MSC function.
source: Some in vitro studies demonstrate a negative impact of cryopreservation on MSC function (François et al., 2012; Chinnadurai et al., 2016); however, others suggest that cryopreservation may not negatively impact their functionality (Cruz et al., 2015; Devaney et al., 2015; Gramlich et al., 2016; Luetzkendorf et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to François et al., 2012 and Chinnadurai et al., 2016.

claim: Some studies suggest that cryopreservation may not negatively impact MSC functionality.
source: Some in vitro studies demonstrate a negative impact of cryopreservation on MSC function (François et al., 2012; Chinnadurai et al., 2016); however, others suggest that cryopreservation may not negatively impact their functionality (Cruz et al., 2015; Devaney et al., 2015; Gramlich et al., 2016; Luetzkendorf et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to multiple studies.

claim: The search strategy yielded 2744 potential studies.
source: The search strategy yielded 2744 potential studies; and after applying the eligibility criteria and full text review, 18 studies were deemed eligible for inclusion (Figure 1; Cruz et al., 2015; Devaney et al., 2015; Gramlich et al., 2016; Salmenkari et al., 2019; Somal et al., 2017; Tan et al., 2019; Curley et al., 2017; Horiuchi et al., 2021; Horie et al., 2021; Yea et al., 2020; Bárcia et al., 2017; Bharti et al., 2020; Khan et al., 2019; Horie et al., 2020a; Lohan et al., 2018; Perlee et al., 2019; Rogulska et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a direct report of the systematic review search results, also shown in Figure 1.

claim: After applying the eligibility criteria and full text review, 18 studies were deemed eligible for inclusion.
source: The search strategy yielded 2744 potential studies; and after applying the eligibility criteria and full text review, 18 studies were deemed eligible for inclusion (Figure 1; Cruz et al., 2015; Devaney et al., 2015; Gramlich et al., 2016; Salmenkari et al., 2019; Somal et al., 2017; Tan et al., 2019; Curley et al., 2017; Horiuchi et al., 2021; Horie et al., 2021; Yea et al., 2020; Bárcia et al., 2017; Bharti et al., 2020; Khan et al., 2019; Horie et al., 2020a; Lohan et al., 2018; Perlee et al., 2019; Rogulska et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a direct report of the systematic review selection process, also shown in Figure 1.

claim: Eight studies used mice for their experiments.
source: Eight studies used mice for their experiments (Cruz et al., 2015; Gramlich et al., 2016; Salmenkari et al., 2019; Somal et al., 2017; Tan et al., 2019; Curley et al., 2017; Perlee et al., 2019; Rogulska et al., 2019), seven studies used rats (Devaney et al., 2015; Curley et al., 2017; Horiuchi et al., 2021; Horie et al., 2021; Yea et al., 2020; Lohan et al., 2018; Horie et al., 2020b), one study used both mice and rats (Bárcia et al., 2017), one study used beagle dogs (Khan et al., 2019), and one study used guinea pigs (Bharti et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a direct report of the animal species used in the included studies.

claim: Seven studies used rats for their experiments.
source: Eight studies used mice for their experiments (Cruz et al., 2015; Gramlich et al., 2016; Salmenkari et al., 2019; Somal et al., 2017; Tan et al., 2019; Curley et al., 2017; Perlee et al., 2019; Rogulska et al., 2019), seven studies used rats (Devaney et al., 2015; Curley et al., 2017; Horiuchi et al., 2021; Horie et al., 2021; Yea et al., 2020; Lohan et al., 2018; Horie et al., 2020b), one study used both mice and rats (Bárcia et al., 2017), one study used beagle dogs (Khan et al., 2019), and one study used guinea pigs (Bharti et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a direct report of the animal species used in the included studies.

claim: One study used both mice and rats.
source: Eight studies used mice for their experiments (Cruz et al., 2015; Gramlich et al., 2016; Salmenkari et al., 2019; Somal et al., 2017; Tan et al., 2019; Curley et al., 2017; Perlee et al., 2019; Rogulska et al., 2019), seven studies used rats (Devaney et al., 2015; Curley et al., 2017; Horiuchi et al., 2021; Horie et al., 2021; Yea et al., 2020; Lohan et al., 2018; Horie et al., 2020b), one study used both mice and rats (Bárcia et al., 2017), one study used beagle dogs (Khan et al., 2019), and one study used guinea pigs (Bharti et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a direct report of the animal species used in the included studies.

claim: One study used beagle dogs.
source: Eight studies used mice for their experiments (Cruz et al., 2015; Gramlich et al., 2016; Salmenkari et al., 2019; Somal et al., 2017; Tan et al., 2019; Curley et al., 2017; Perlee et al., 2019; Rogulska et al., 2019), seven studies used rats (Devaney et al., 2015; Curley et al., 2017; Horiuchi et al., 2021; Horie et al., 2021; Yea et al., 2020; Lohan et al., 2018; Horie et al., 2020b), one study used both mice and rats (Bárcia et al., 2017), one study used beagle dogs (Khan et al., 2019), and one study used guinea pigs (Bharti et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a direct report of the animal species used in the included studies.

claim: One study used guinea pigs.
source: Eight studies used mice for their experiments (Cruz et al., 2015; Gramlich et al., 2016; Salmenkari et al., 2019; Somal et al., 2017; Tan et al., 2019; Curley et al., 2017; Perlee et al., 2019; Rogulska et al., 2019), seven studies used rats (Devaney et al., 2015; Curley et al., 2017; Horiuchi et al., 2021; Horie et al., 2021; Yea et al., 2020; Lohan et al., 2018; Horie et al., 2020b), one study used both mice and rats (Bárcia et al., 2017), one study used beagle dogs (Khan et al., 2019), and one study used guinea pigs (Bharti et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a direct report of the animal species used in the included studies.

claim: Twelve studies included a 'vehicle only' as an additional control arm.
source: Twelve studies included a 'vehicle only' as an additional control arm (Devaney et al., 2015; Gramlich et al., 2016; Salmenkari et al., 2019; Somal et al., 2017; Horiuchi et al., 2021; Horie et al., 2021; Yea et al., 2020; Bharti et al., 2020; Lohan et al., 2018; Perlee et al., 2019; Rogulska et al., 2019; Horie et al., 2020b), while four studies employed a sham animal model, where disease negative animals received MSCs or vehicle (Tan et al., 2019; Curley et al., 2017; Bárcia et al., 2017; Horie et al., 2020a).
evidence: This is a direct report of the control groups used in the included studies.

claim: Four studies employed a sham animal model, where disease negative animals received MSCs or vehicle.
source: Twelve studies included a 'vehicle only' as an additional control arm (Devaney et al., 2015; Gramlich et al., 2016; Salmenkari et al., 2019; Somal et al., 2017; Horiuchi et al., 2021; Horie et al., 2021; Yea et al., 2020; Bharti et al., 2020; Lohan et al., 2018; Perlee et al., 2019; Rogulska et al., 2019; Horie et al., 2020b), while four studies employed a sham animal model, where disease negative animals received MSCs or vehicle (Tan et al., 2019; Curley et al., 2017; Bárcia et al., 2017; Horie et al., 2020a).
evidence: This is a direct report of the control groups used in the included studies.

claim: Seven studies studied models of preclinical lung injury and sepsis.
source: Of the 18 included studies, seven studied models of preclinical lung injury and sepsis (Devaney et al., 2015; Tan et al., 2019; Curley et al., 2017; Horie et al., 2021; Horie et al., 2020a; Perlee et al., 2019; Horie et al., 2020b), four a wound healing model (Somal et al., 2017; Yea et al., 2020; Bharti et al., 2020; Rogulska et al., 2019), three of neurological or ocular disease, specifically one of corneal transplantation (Lohan et al., 2018), retinal ischemia/reperfusion (Gramlich et al., 2016), and spinal cord injury model (Khan et al., 2019), and one each of allergic airway inflammatory disease (Cruz et al., 2015), wound healing and chronic inflammatory arthritis (Bárcia et al., 2017), acute and chronic inflammatory colitis (Salmenkari et al., 2019), and chronic osteoarthritis (Horiuchi et al., 2021).
evidence: This is a direct report of the disease models used in the included studies.

claim: Four studies used a wound healing model.
source: Of the 18 included studies, seven studied models of preclinical lung injury and sepsis (Devaney et al., 2015; Tan et al., 2019; Curley et al., 2017; Horie et al., 2021; Horie et al., 2020a; Perlee et al., 2019; Horie et al., 2020b), four a wound healing model (Somal et al., 2017; Yea et al., 2020; Bharti et al., 2020; Rogulska et al., 2019), three of neurological or ocular disease, specifically one of corneal transplantation (Lohan et al., 2018), retinal ischemia/reperfusion (Gramlich et al., 2016), and spinal cord injury model (Khan et al., 2019), and one each of allergic airway inflammatory disease (Cruz et al., 2015), wound healing and chronic inflammatory arthritis (Bárcia et al., 2017), acute and chronic inflammatory colitis (Salmenkari et al., 2019), and chronic osteoarthritis (Horiuchi et al., 2021).
evidence: This is a direct report of the disease models used in the included studies.

claim: Ten studies used 10% DMSO as part of their cryopreservation solution.
source: Ten studies used 10% DMSO (dimethyl sulfoxide) as part of their cryopreservation solution (Cruz et al., 2015; Devaney et al., 2015; Salmenkari et al., 2019; Somal et al., 2017; Yea et al., 2020; Bárcia et al., 2017; Bharti et al., 2020; Khan et al., 2019; Lohan et al., 2018; Rogulska et al., 2019), three studies used CryoStor Cell Preservation Media (Sigma-Aldrich) (Gramlich et al., 2016; Horie et al., 2021; Horie et al., 2020a), one study used MSC Freezing media (Biological Industries) (Tan et al., 2019), one study used 5% DMSO (Horiuchi et al., 2021), and three studies did not report the solution used for cryopreservation (Curley et al., 2017; Perlee et al., 2019; Horie et al., 2020b).
evidence: This is a direct report of the cryopreservation methods used in the included studies.

claim: Of the 166 experiments on organ dysfunction and/or composition of tissue outcomes, only one reported a significant difference at the 0.05 level or less between the freshly cultured and cryopreserved MSC groups which favoured the cryopreserved group.
source: Of the 116 experiments, only one reported a significant difference at the 0.05 level or less between the freshly cultured and cryopreserved MSC groups which favoured the cryopreserved group (Figure 2).
evidence: This is a direct report of the statistical analysis results, also shown in Figure 2.

claim: Seventeen studies reported post-thaw viability of cryopreserved MSCs, with a range from 60% to 98% across various time points since thawing.
source: Seventeen studies (Cruz et al., 2015; Devaney et al., 2015; Gramlich et al., 2016; Somal et al., 2017; Tan et al., 2019; Curley et al., 2017; Horiuchi et al., 2021; Horie et al., 2021; Yea et al., 2020; Bárcia et al., 2017; Bharti et al., 2020; Khan et al., 2019; Horie et al., 2020a; Lohan et al., 2018; Perlee et al., 2019; Rogulska et al., 2019; Horie et al., 2020b) reported post-thaw viability of cryopreserved MSCs, the range was from 60% to 98% across various time points since thawing.
evidence: This is a direct report of viability data from the included studies.

claim: The viability of freshly cultured MSCs ranged from 91% to 99%, assessed at various time points.
source: The viability of freshly cultured MSCs ranged from 91% to 99%, also assessed at various time points.
evidence: This is a direct report of viability data from the included studies.

claim: Of the 25 viability experiments comparing freshly cultured and cryopreserved MSCs, 9 (36%) favoured freshly cultured MSCs.
source: Of the 25 experiments, 9 (36%) favoured freshly cultured MSCs (Figure 5).
evidence: This is a direct report of the statistical analysis results, also shown in Figure 5.

claim: 251 out of 257 (97.6%) of the in vivo pre-clinical efficacy outcomes demonstrated no statistically significant differences between cryopreserved and freshly cultured MSCs at a p value of<0.05.
source: Across the 18 included studies, our review found that 251 out of 257 (97.6%) of the in vivo pre-clinical efficacy outcomes demonstrated no statistically significant differences between cryopreserved and freshly cultured MSCs at a p value of<0.05.
evidence: This is a direct report of the statistical analysis results from the systematic review.

claim: Cryopreserved MSCs have a higher percentage of apoptotic cells than MSCs from fresh cultures.
source: Cryopreserved MSCs have a higher percentage of apoptotic cells than MSCs from fresh cultures (Haack-Sørensen and Kastrup, 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Haack-Sørensen and Kastrup, 2011.

claim: Apoptotic and necrotic pathways are activated in MSCs 6–48 h post-thaw in response to low temperature exposure.
source: Apoptotic and necrotic pathways are activated in these cells 6–48 h post-thaw in response to low temperature exposure (Chinnadurai et al., 2016; Baust et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Chinnadurai et al., 2016 and Baust et al., 2009.

claim: At least 90% viability for fresh MSC product and 70% viability for cryopreserved MSC product are considered the benchmark for pre-clinical application.
source: Viability of MSCs is considered an important indicator of cryopreservation success where at least 90% viability for fresh MSC product and 70% viability for cryopreserved MSC product are considered the benchmark for pre-clinical application (Robb et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Robb et al., 2019.

claim: Recipient cytotoxic cell activity causing apoptosis of infused MSCs or infusion of ex-vivo apoptotic MSCs is one of the proposed mechanisms of immunomodulation for MSCs.
source: One provocative study found that recipient cytotoxic cell activity causing apoptosis of infused MSCs or infusion of ex-vivo apoptotic MSCs and suggested it is one of the proposed mechanisms of immunomodulation for MSCs and the lower viability (or increased number of apoptotic cells) may in fact play a positive role in reducing the host inflammatory state (Galleu et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Galleu et al., 2017.

claim: In a safety systematic review of MSC randomized trials, only 52% and 14.5% reported on viability and potency respectively.
source: In a safety systematic review of MSC randomized trials, only 52% and 14.5% reported on viability and potency respectively (Thompson et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Thompson et al., 2020.

claim: 13 of 18 included studies received an 'unclear' risk of bias in 5 out of 10 domains of the SYRCLE risk of bias tool due to insufficient and unclear reporting of important variables.
source: Our systematic review also found that 13 of 18 included studies received an "unclear" risk of bias in 5 out of 10 domains of the SYRCLE risk of bias tool due to insufficient and unclear reporting of important variables (eg. cryopreservation process, storage conditions, blinding, etc.).
evidence: This is a direct report of the risk of bias assessment results from the systematic review.

claim: A phase III randomized clinical trial showed that high risk patients with acute graft-versus-host disease were more likely to have a partial response at 28 days with Remestemcel-L (a cryopreserved MSC product).
source: From the perspective of clinical research and potential efficacy of cryopreserved MSCs, a phase III randomized clinical trial that examined whether a cryopreserved MSC product, PROCHYMAL (Remestemcel-L), or placebo compared to standard second line therapies alone in children with acute graft-versus-host disease (aGVHD) showed that high risk patients were more likely to have a partial response at 28 days with Remestemcel.
evidence: This is a report of findings from a phase III clinical trial.

claim: Of the 15 trials that studied a cryopreserved MSC product, 5 of them (33%) found significant differences favoring cryopreserved MSCs in either the primary or secondary endpoints.
source: Of the 15 trials that studied a cryopreserved product, 5 of them (33%) found significant differences favoring cryopreserved MSCs in either the primary or secondary endpoints (Kebriaei et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Kebriaei et al., 2020.

claim: The protocol for the systematic review is published in Systematic Reviews and registered in PROSPERO (CRD42020145833).
source: The protocol for our systematic review is published in Systematic Reviews (https://doi.org/10.1186/s13643-020-01437-z) and registered in PROSPERO (CRD42020145833).
evidence: This is a factual statement about the publication and registration of the review protocol.

claim: Electronic search strategies were conducted on Ovid platform, Ovid MEDLINE, OvidMEDLINE In-Process & Other Non-Indexed Citations, Embase Classic plus Embase, and BIOSIS and Web of Science using Web of Knowledge until January 13, 2022.
source: We conducted electronic search strategies without language restriction of Ovid platform, Ovid MEDLINE, OvidMEDLINE In-Process & Other Non-Indexed Citations, Embase Classic plus Embase, and BIOSIS and Web of Science using Web of Knowledge until January 13, 2022.
evidence: This is a direct report of the search methodology used in the systematic review.

claim: Risk of bias was assessed using the SYRCLE 'Risk of Bias' assessment tool for pre-clinical in vivo studies.
source: All studies were assessed as high, low, or unclear for the 10 domains of bias adapted from the SYRCLE 'Risk of Bias' assessment tool for pre-clinical in vivo studies (Hooijmans et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a direct report of the risk of bias assessment methodology, supported by a citation to Hooijmans et al., 2014.

claim: None of the 18 included studies met low-risk of bias criteria for all 10 domains.
source: Of the 18 included studies, none of them met low-risk of bias criteria for all 10 domains and all studies demonstrated unclear risk of bias due to lack or reporting in atleast two domains.
evidence: This is a direct report of the risk of bias assessment results.

claim: All 18 included studies demonstrated unclear risk of bias due to lack of reporting in at least two domains.
source: Of the 18 included studies, none of them met low-risk of bias criteria for all 10 domains and all studies demonstrated unclear risk of bias due to lack or reporting in atleast two domains.
evidence: This is a direct report of the risk of bias assessment results.

claim: Ten studies did not have any features that would confer a high-risk of bias in one of the 10 domains.
source: Ten studies did not have any features that would confer a high-risk of bias in the one of the 10 domains (Cruz et al., 2015; Devaney et al., 2015; Tan et al., 2019; Curley et al., 2017; Horiuchi et al., 2021; Horie et al., 2021; Yea et al., 2020; Bharti et al., 2020; Khan et al., 2019; Horie et al., 2020a).
evidence: This is a direct report of the risk of bias assessment results.

claim: Seventeen studies assessed composition of tissues as an in vivo pre-clinical efficacy outcome.
source: Seventeen studies assessed composition of tissues (Cruz et al., 2015; Devaney et al., 2015; Gramlich et al., 2016; Salmenkari et al., 2019; Somal et al., 2017; Tan et al., 2019; Curley et al., 2017; Horiuchi et al., 2021; Horie et al., 2021; Yea et al., 2020; Bárcia et al., 2017; Bharti et al., 2020; Khan et al., 2019; Horie et al., 2020a; Lohan et al., 2018; Perlee et al., 2019; Rogulska et al., 2019), and 12 assessed organ dysfunction (Cruz et al., 2015; Devaney et al., 2015; Gramlich et al., 2016; Salmenkari et al., 2019; Curley et al., 2017; Horiuchi et al., 2021; Horie et al., 2021; Yea et al., 2020; Bárcia et al., 2017; Khan et al., 2019; Horie et al., 2020a; Horie et al., 2020b).
evidence: This is a direct report of the outcome measures assessed in the included studies.

claim: Twelve studies assessed organ dysfunction as an in vivo pre-clinical efficacy outcome.
source: Seventeen studies assessed composition of tissues (Cruz et al., 2015; Devaney et al., 2015; Gramlich et al., 2016; Salmenkari et al., 2019; Somal et al., 2017; Tan et al., 2019; Curley et al., 2017; Horiuchi et al., 2021; Horie et al., 2021; Yea et al., 2020; Bárcia et al., 2017; Bharti et al., 2020; Khan et al., 2019; Horie et al., 2020a; Lohan et al., 2018; Perlee et al., 2019; Rogulska et al., 2019), and 12 assessed organ dysfunction (Cruz et al., 2015; Devaney et al., 2015; Gramlich et al., 2016; Salmenkari et al., 2019; Curley et al., 2017; Horiuchi et al., 2021; Horie et al., 2021; Yea et al., 2020; Bárcia et al., 2017; Khan et al., 2019; Horie et al., 2020a; Horie et al., 2020b).
evidence: This is a direct report of the outcome measures assessed in the included studies.

claim: Eleven studies assessed protein expression and secretion as an in vivo pre-clinical efficacy outcome.
source: Eleven of the 18 studies assessed protein expression and secretion (Cruz et al., 2015; Devaney et al., 2015; Salmenkari et al., 2019; Tan et al., 2019; Curley et al., 2017; Horiuchi et al., 2021; Khan et al., 2019; Horie et al., 2020a; Lohan et al., 2018; Perlee et al., 2019; Horie et al., 2020b) (Table 2).
evidence: This is a direct report of the outcome measures assessed in the included studies.

claim: Fifteen studies reported in vitro potency outcomes, including viability.
source: Fifteen studies reported in vitro potency outcomes, including viability (Cruz et al., 2015; Devaney et al., 2015; Gramlich et al., 2016; Somal et al., 2017; Tan et al., 2019; Curley et al., 2017; Horiuchi et al., 2021; Bárcia et al., 2017; Bharti et al., 2020; Khan et al., 2019; Horie et al., 2020a; Lohan et al., 2018; Perlee et al., 2019; Rogulska et al., 2019; Horie et al., 2020b) with 68 experiments and 32 different outcome measures.
evidence: This is a direct report of the outcome measures assessed in the included studies.

claim: Three studies reported in vitro co-culture assay outcomes (7 separate experiments) to assess the impact of MSCs on responder cell proliferation.
source: Three studies reported in vitro co-culture assay outcomes (7 separate experiments) to assess the impact of MSCs on responder cell proliferation (Gramlich et al., 2016; Tan et al., 2019; Bárcia et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a direct report of the outcome measures assessed in the included studies.

claim: All three co-culture assay studies found no significant difference in potency for cryopreserved as compared to freshly-cultured MSCs at varying concentrations of MSCs to responder cells.
source: All three studies found no significant difference in potency for cryopreserved as compared to freshly-cultured MSCs at varying concentrations of MSCs to responder cells (Table 7).
evidence: This is a direct report of the statistical analysis results from the included studies.

claim: The ability to conduct meta-analyses on primary outcome measures was significantly limited by the heterogeneity of animal models included and breadth of outcomes measured.
source: Our ability to conduct meta-analyses on our primary outcome measures and according to subgroups was significantly limited by the heterogeneity of animal models included and breadth of outcomes measured.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of the systematic review methodology.

claim: The systematic review was designed and conducted using a pre-published protocol to enhance transparency and reproducibility.
source: However, we designed and then conducted a systematic and transparent search using a pre-published protocol to enhance transparency and reproducibility, and to ensure we captured the totality of the evidence according to our study question.
evidence: This is a statement about the methodology of the systematic review.
